name: Rhus

project_scope.note: Approved B008 Central Texas sumac set. Rhus copallinum var. lanceolata retains Rhus lanceolata as a prominent synonym. Rhus trilobata is treated within current Rhus aromatica. Rhus microphylla is also canonical as a RANGE_UNRESOLVED learner entry; do not count it in confirmed-native metrics.

shared_traits: woody shrubs or small trees with alternate compound leaves
resinous/aromatic tissues common in the family
fruit and leaf architecture are more useful than flower color
priority: distinguish three-leaflet Rhus aromatica from Toxicodendron radicans
study_strategy.warning: Do not teach 'leaves of three = poison ivy.' Rhus aromatica also has three leaflets. Do not use sap contact or crushing as an identification test.
study_strategy.look_here_first: Count leaflets on a complete leaf, then inspect whether the central leaf axis (rachis) has a leafy wing. Compare leaflet size, margin, and whether foliage persists in winter. Confirm using flowers or drupes when present.

quick_key.if: many narrow leaflets + conspicuously winged rachis + deciduous small tree/shrub
5–9 thick glossy entire leaflets + evergreen/semi-evergreen shrub
several very small dull green leaflets + densely branched dry-site shrub; rachis may be narrowly winged
quick_key.then: Rhus microphylla (range unresolved; do not identify by thorns alone)

quick_key.if: exactly 3 often lobed/coarsely toothed leaflets + low deciduous suckering shrub

b066_study_strategy.warning: Current Kew treats R. trilobata as a synonym of R. aromatica var. aromatica. Do not maintain duplicate species/variety learners.

quick_split: R. aromatica — exactly 3 larger fan-shaped/lobed leaflets; low suckering shrub; local PASS.
R. microphylla — several much smaller leaflets on a pinnate leaf; dry western/southwestern shrub; range HOLD.

species_comparison_matrix.R. aromatica: trifoliolate; leaflets often lobed or toothed
species_comparison_matrix.R. copallinum var. lanceolata: pinnate, narrow leaflets, conspicuously winged rachis
species_comparison_matrix.R. microphylla: pinnate, very small leaflets; rachis sometimes narrowly winged
species_comparison_matrix.R. virens: pinnate, leathery, glossy, mostly entire leaflets

species_comparison_matrix.R. microphylla: densely branched shrub, often dry western habitats
leaflet size with scale and rachis detail
species_comparison_matrix.R. virens: thick entire glossy leaflets and their attachment

comparison_cautions: A narrow rachis wing may occur in R. microphylla; conspicuous wings plus larger narrow leaflets favor R. copallinum var. lanceolata.
Do not rely on absence of spines alone for R. microphylla; branch-tip spinescence reports need targeted diagnostic review.
R. aromatica and poison ivy (Toxicodendron radicans) both have three leaflets; compare habit, leaflet margin, fruit and stem attachment without touching sap.
R. trilobata names remain represented under R. aromatica, not separate canonical taxa.
R. microphylla is installed for study but its target-zone range status remains unresolved.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched whole leaves of all four species on millimeter grids showing leaflet counts
R. aromatica: leaf junction and leaflet lobes, with poison ivy look-alike comparison
R. copallinum var. lanceolata: rachis wing close-up and whole leaf
R. microphylla: tiny leaflet measurements, rachis wing variation and branch-tip close-up
R. virens: leaf texture and entire leaflet margins with scale
All four: fruit clusters and close-ups of drupes where available
